hypothesis: If the claim holds, domestic dog genomes will fall into two or more lineages that are each closer to different wild canid species than to one another, not form a single clade nested within one wild species.
pass_criterion: Phylogeny or admixture analysis of whole-genome data shows dogs splitting into >= 2 lineages whose most recent common ancestors are separate wild species, with divergence between those lineages greater than within-wolf diversity (>1 Myr).
fail_criterion: All domestic dogs form one monophyletic clade nested in Canis lupus, with no deep split between dog lineages and other Canis species (jackal, coyote) contributing only minor admixture (<5%).
interpretation: 'Several wild species' means several biological species of Canis or related canids. The modern test is nuclear and mitochondrial genome ancestry. Introgression from other canids does not count as multiple origins unless it provides the main ancestry.

dataset.name: NCBI Genome: Canis lupus familiaris
dataset.why_it_fits: Provides dog reference assemblies and links to wolf, coyote and jackal assemblies and SRA resequencing runs needed for phylogenetic and admixture analysis.
